title: The Law of Reflection
lead: Every reflection, from a mirror, a lake or a sheet of paper, obeys one simple law: the angle of reflection equals the angle of incidence, both measured from the perpendicular to the surface. A smooth surface sends parallel rays off in one direction, while a rough surface diffuses them in many. The same law places the image in a flat mirror as far behind the mirror as the object stands in front of it.
objectives: Explain reflection of light from polished and rough surfaces.
summary_html:
• The angle of reflection equals the angle of incidence.
  • A mirror has a smooth surface and reflects light at specific angles.
  • Light is diffused when it reflects from a rough surface.
  • Mirror images can be photographed and videotaped by instruments.

figures.original_caption: The law of reflection states that the angle of reflection equals the angle of incidence— $\theta_{\text{r}} = \theta_{\text{i}}$. The angles are measured relative to the perpendicular to the surface at the point where the ray strikes the surface.

(Figure 25.5) Light is diffused when it reflects from a rough surface. Here many parallel rays are incident, but they are reflected at many different angles since the surface is rough. (Figure 25.6) When a sheet of paper is illuminated with many parallel incident rays, it can be seen at many different angles, because its surface is rough and diffuses the light. (Figure 25.7) A mirror illuminated by many parallel rays reflects them in only one direction, since its surface is very smooth. Only the observer at a particular angle will see the reflected light.

Our image in a mirror is behind the mirror. The two rays shown are those that strike the mirror at just the correct angles to be reflected into the eyes of the person. The image appears to be in the direction the rays are coming from when they enter the eyes.

exercises.prompt: Using the law of reflection, explain how powder takes the shine off of a person’s nose. What is the name of the optical effect?

answer.solution: Skin with a film of oil on it is smooth compared with the wavelength of light, so it acts like a small mirror. Each ray obeys the law of reflection at the same smooth surface, the reflected rays all leave in nearly one direction, and an observer at that angle sees a bright highlight, the shine. Powder is made of many tiny grains, and their surfaces face every which way. Each ray still obeys the law of reflection, but at a grain tilted differently from its neighbors, so the reflected rays leave in many directions. The light is spread out instead of concentrated into a highlight, and the nose looks evenly lit from every angle. The effect is diffuse reflection, or diffusion.

exercises.prompt: An object is 2 meters in front of a flat mirror. Ray 1 from the object travels in a direction toward the mirror and normal to the mirror’s surface. Ray 2 from the object travels at an angle of 5° from the direction of ray 1, and it also reflects off the mirror’s surface. At what distance behind the mirror do these two reflected rays appear to converge to form an image?

answer.hint: Ray 1 comes straight back, and ray 2 leaves the mirror at the same 5° it arrived at. Trace both back behind the mirror and find where they cross.

figure.alt: A man standing in front of a mirror on a wall at a distance of several feet. The mirror’s top is at eye level, but its bottom is only waist high. Arrows illustrate how the man can see his reflection from head to toe in the mirror.
figure.caption: A full-length mirror is one in which you can see all of yourself. It need not be as big as you, and its size is independent of your distance from it.

exercises.prompt: Suppose a man stands in front of a mirror as shown in the figure. His eyes are 1.65 m above the floor, and the top of his head is 0.13 m higher. Find the height above the floor of the top and bottom of the smallest mirror in which he can see both the top of his head and his feet. How is this distance related to the man’s height?

parts.part: the top of the mirror above the floor
parts.hint: By the law of reflection, the ray from the top of his head reaches the mirror halfway between his head and his eyes.

parts.part: the bottom of the mirror above the floor
parts.hint: The ray from his feet reaches the mirror halfway between the floor and his eyes.

answer.solution: Top $1.715\text{ m}$ from floor, bottom $0.825\text{ m}$ from floor. Height of mirror is $0.890\text{ m}$, or precisely one-half the height of the person.
